lines: In nineteen ninety-one, two hikers in the Alps found a body sticking out of the ice.
They thought it was a climber who had died recently.
He was about *five thousand three hundred* years old.
The ice froze and slowly dried his body, so even his skin and organs survived.
Scientists named him {Otzi|ER1 T S IY0}. He has sixty-one tattoos, made of simple lines and crosses.
Most sit near worn joints and his lower back. [pause 100] They may have been a treatment for pain.
His stomach had moved upward as he dried, so it was missed for years.
His last meal was still inside: [pause 100] ibex and deer meat, ancient wheat, and a toxic fern.
It also held {H.|EY1 CH} {pylori|P AY0 L AO1 R IY0}, a bacterium that still causes stomach ulcers today.
Then, in two thousand and one, an X-ray showed a stone arrowhead in his left shoulder.
It cut a major artery. [pause 100] He most likely bled to death on the mountain.
A deep cut on his hand suggests he had been in a fight days before.
Today he is kept in a cold room at a museum in Italy, still frozen.
